question: Time to MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, modelled by Cox regression. Both models combine the MRI channel with clinical and cognitive scales. P-13 uses longitudinal CDRSB and hippocampal-volume trajectories plus baseline ADAS13, MMSE, RAVLT, FAQ, demographics and APOE e4. P-1128 uses baseline T1 cortical morphology and grey-matter network radiomics plus MoCA and FAQ. The population class is the same (Alzheimer's-spectrum MCI in ADNI). P-13's figure comes from a high-risk subgroup defined by clustering longitudinal FAQ trajectories, and P-1128's sample keeps converters within 60 months and patients stable for 5 years. Those are cohort-selection differences, which the rule allows. P-524, P-574 and P-940 are named in the record only as context for a registry repair class and carry no compared quantity.

figures.P-13: High-risk subgroup (n = 340; 80.9% LMCI), random split 237/103. Training C-index 0.844 (95% CI 0.815-0.873, SE about 0.0148), optimism-corrected 0.829, test set 0.805 with no interval. The number of converters in the test split is not printed. Hanley-McNeil applied to the C-index, over 30-70 events of 103: SE 0.042-0.052, giving about 0.70-0.72 to 0.89-0.91 (for 50/53: SE 0.0437, 0.719-0.891).
figures.P-1128: 162 ADNI MCI (68 converters within 6-60 months, 94 stable at 5 years, reverters excluded), random split 112/50. Morphology-network-clinical model: training 0.951 (0.928-0.974, SE about 0.0117); validation 0.880 (0.817-0.943, SE about 0.032). For reference, Hanley-McNeil with about 21 converters and 29 stable in validation gives SE 0.053 (0.776-0.984), wider than the printed interval.
figures.comparison: Training against training, both apparent: the intervals exclude each other (0.815-0.873 against 0.928-0.974); z = 0.107/sqrt(0.0148^2 + 0.0117^2) = 5.7. Hold-out against hold-out: P-13's 0.805 lies below P-1128's printed interval by 0.012, but 0.880 lies inside P-13's derived interval at any plausible event count; z = 0.075/sqrt(0.0437^2 + 0.032^2) = 1.4. The record's own comparison (P-13's training 0.844 against P-1128's validation 0.880) is not like for like.

matched_figure_check: No figure reconciles the pair. On the single-timepoint input (P-1128's condition), P-13's only baseline figures are single-assessment models in the high-risk group, best ADAS13 at 0.677/0.665. These are lower still, so they widen the gap rather than close it. P-13 reports no C-index for its model in all MCI or truncated at 60 months (calibration plots at 1, 3 and 5 years only). P-1128 reports no C-index inside a high-risk subgroup (only a median-split KM curve) and no longitudinal model.
performance_validity: Passes. The highest figure is P-1128's training 0.951, below 0.97, and its compared hold-out figure is 0.880; P-13's are 0.805-0.844. P-1128 has no external cohort and selects 37 of 1,474 radiomic features by univariate Cox and LASSO, with no statement that selection was confined to the training set. That is recorded as a candidate explanation, not an exclusion.

candidate_explanations.difference: Population subset: P-13's estimate is confined to a high-risk subgroup identified from follow-up FAQ trajectories (80.9% late MCI). Restricting the risk range in this way would lower discrimination.
candidate_explanations.quote: Thus, HDDC was performed to identify the risk groups based on FAQ. The high- and low-risk groups included 340 and 378 individuals with MCI, respectively.

candidate_explanations.difference: Case selection in P-1128: only converters within 60 months and patients stable for 5 years, with reverters excluded, so intermediate cases are left out.
candidate_explanations.quote: The dataset included baseline T1W images and clinical data of 68 MCI patients who progressed to AD in 6–60 months and 94 other MCI patients without AD conversion in 5 years

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation within the channel: longitudinal trajectory scores (MFPCA of CDRSB and hippocampal volume) plus baseline cognition and APOE e4, against baseline cortical morphology and network radiomics plus MoCA and FAQ.
candidate_explanations.quote: five functional principal components were extracted by MFPCA, namely rho1 to rho5, which capture the essential information in the CDRSB and hippocampal longitudinal markers.

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon: visits to 96 months in P-13 against conversion within 60 months in P-1128.
candidate_explanations.quote: A total of 718 individuals were assessed at baseline and at 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, and 96 months of follow-up.

candidate_explanations.difference: Feature selection and validation: selection from 1,474 features by univariate Cox and LASSO with no statement that it was confined to the training set, a 50-patient hold-out and no external validation. P-1128's training-to-validation drop is 0.071, against 0.039 in P-13.
candidate_explanations.quote: Second, the 37 features with significant differences (p < 0.05) were chosen using univariate Cox analysis.

candidate_explanations.difference: Sample size: 103-patient test split against 50-patient validation split.
candidate_explanations.quote: The high-risk MCI dataset (n = 340) was randomly split into a training set (n = 237) and test set (n = 103).

reason: Same question (ADNI MCI-to-AD conversion, MRI plus clinical data, C-index) and no matched figure: P-13's own single-timepoint figures are lower still. The gap exceeds uncertainty in both directions only on the apparent training estimates (0.844 against 0.951, z = 5.7). On the held-out estimates, P-13's 0.805 falls 0.012 below P-1128's printed interval, but P-1128's 0.880 lies inside P-13's derived interval (z = 1.4). The pair therefore meets condition 4 as worded, but at the fairer tier only in one direction, hence borderline. The candidate explanations (high-risk subgroup, extreme-case selection, input representation, horizon, feature selection without stated split confinement) are not shown to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: The C-index of the model was 0.844 (95% CI: 0.815–0.873), and the optimism- corrected C-index by bootstrapping was 0.829. In addition, the C- index of the test set was 0.805 (see details in Table 4).
For the high-risk group, in the baseline models, ADAS13 showed the best performance (C-index/Optimism-corrected C-index = 0.677/ 0.665).
In the follow-up period, participants with bidirectional changes (MCI to AD and back to MCI) were excluded.
Second, our research lacked independent external validation.
Third, this study did not analyze dynamic follow-up data.
